_about: Step 3m B8: every tunable number of the decision engine and the trainer, by difficulty. Age stays in the ratings (step 3l), never here. Tune only these and the evaluation constants against the exam (B9); never ratings or rules.

eval._about: Evaluation constants (game units). responses_per_defender: k in B3. later_p: the delivery chance of a look that needs another offence turn (the defence may still answer it). continuation: the share of the best residual threat the leaf credits (the rest is the chance the possession doesn't reach it).
eval._fouls: Step 3n F4: the engine's estimate of the defence's fouls per possession and the value of playing on after a +5 steal foul, used to price a foul over the rest of the quarter. Tune from the F5 run, never the rules.
eval._settle_shots: Step 18b; on by default for every level since D-148 (Shaun, 11 Nov 2026; checked at Rookie and Starter in step 18c). (1) A position with a shot declared is valued at the search's horizon by playing the reaction out by the rules: the defence's best legal reply (a Contest, a movement to the shooter and then a Contest, a Steal, or nothing), the dice at their chances. (2) D-145: no reading is above the most the possession can still earn (what it has earned plus the best open shot any attacker's card can score), before or after the calibrated map. (3) The quicker reading that orders the list of turns goes through the same ceiling and map, so a settled shot and a position that plays on are ranked on one scale.
eval._calibrated: Step 17D; on by default for every level since D-138 (Shaun, 11 Nov 2026): the calibrated reading. Today's reading of what a position has left to earn is passed through a map fitted to what positions went on to earn, per phase and side to act (data/learned_weights.json, calibration; one file for both engines). Fitted, not hand-set (D-137). The map was fitted on Senior Pro play; another age and standard scales it by its own phase table value over Senior Pro's at the same phase, as D-114 (step 18a). Under the table's rules the file's calibration_tabletop map is used: fitted the same way on tabletop-rules play (D-141).
eval._help_readings: Step 18c (off). The floor: with the offence to act in open play, a position is worth at least the best shot the ball handler can release this turn (his shot from where he stands, or after one movement), settled by the rules against the defence's best reaction. The reading names the candidates; the rules value them.
eval._learned: Step 17 (off): the learned judgement. What a position has left to earn is read from the named readings (decide.FEATURES) with per-phase weights fitted to how possessions went on (data/learned_weights.json, one file for both engines), in place of the hand-combined reading.
eval._advantages: Step 16, goals stage 3 (off): each team turn the offence's advantages are read from the board (separation, mismatch, numbers, penetration: decide.Read.advantages) and recorded with their stage, target look, chance and worth. Reading and recording only: no choice changes.
eval._coverage_budget: Step 13 B (off): coverage as a budget. In one team turn a defender attends one attacker; the defence splits each defender across the attackers he can answer, and the offence's value is its best look after the defence's best shares (an exact small linear program, decide.Read.budget). With it, the ball handler's looks also count the squares he reaches in two actions by the movement rules (D-115), and the position value is read against relative_average_budget.
eval._reach: Steps 12 and 13 (D-121): the reach map, on by default. Who can Contest in time, who can step into a pass and who reaches an attacker's path are read by the exact movement rules.
eval._relative: D-92 (Shaun, 10 Nov 2026): leaf_mode relative (the default: the phase table plus how much this position's continuation read beats the average at its phase) or floor. relative_average per age/standard and phase from tools/relative_average.py (D-114): Senior Pro is the base; other levels scale it by their phase table over Senior Pro's, and use their own average once they have 100 positions at the phase (provisional); relative_average_source says which
eval._relative_budget: Step 13 B: the averages the position value is read against when coverage_budget is on: the same positions and rule as relative_average (D-114), read with coverage as a budget (tools/relative_average.py --budget)

trainer._about: Step 3m Part D. Bands in game units of value lost; calibrate from stored games.
trainer._level_median_loss: The median value lost per decision by each computer level, graded by the All-Star search: a human moves up when theirs is at or below their current level's. Calibrate from stored games.
trainer._accuracy_k: Step 3n E: per-decision accuracy 100 x exp(-loss / k); calibrated so All-Star's own decisions average about 90, Starter's 75, Rookie's 55 (tools/accuracy_3n.py).
trainer._anchors: Step 3n H: from self-play (Rookie v Starter, Starter v All-Star, Rookie v All-Star; 12 matches of 4 possessions each, Senior Pro digital, tools/anchors_3n.py): gaps fitted to the match scores. Youth and junior keep the senior gaps, 20 and 50 lower as before.

search._open_list: Step 18e (D-156): the list of turns without the hand-written choice of which actions to consider: every legal action is read and only the reading decides what goes forward (search.open_turns_x in search.py, openTurnsX in engine.js). open_list: null = each level's own setting (profiles.<level>.open_list: every level plays 'defence' since step 18f, D-157); false = off for every level; 'defence' = the defence's list; 'both' = the offence's too (every legal offence action read in full: slow, measured only). open_full: the full reads taken for each first action followed, beyond the list's length. open_follow: first actions followed for each one the old list followed. A level may set its own open_full and open_follow (step 18f: the Rookie 2 and 1, the Starter 4 and 2, the All-Star these), because how many turns a level reads in full is how well it chooses.
search._whole_turns: Step 18f (D-159): a one-action turn is valued as the turn ended there, so the other side has the reply the rules give it before the position is judged. On: it won its head to head (+1.7 points a pair, 0.3 to 3.1, 400 pairs).
search._split_ties: Step 18f (D-159): turns that read exactly the same are put in order by the other side's next-best replies (the turn that leaves it the worst second choice first), and share one draw of the pick noise, so chance no longer chooses between them. On: 149 pairs won to 111 lost of 400 (57 in 100 of the decided pairs, 51 to 63); +1.2 points a pair (-0.3 to 2.7).
search._about: Steps 12 and 13: the stable search, in five switches (stable is the shorthand that turns on all five). On by default: like_with_like (D-121). Off: quiet_points, clear_reason and tempo (D-122). play_on is RETIRED (D-149, Shaun, 11 Nov 2026): eval.settle_shots replaced it; the code stays only because the engines' agreement tests turn all five parts on together; don't switch it on. quiet_points: look-ahead counts completed team turns, a side is never judged between its two actions. like_with_like: the answer comes from the deepest even depth (an offence turn and the reply). tempo: each reading is shifted by half of tempo_gap toward the side not to act (tempo_gap: the measured gap between the same position with the offence and with the defence to act, tools/stable_measures.py; D-119). play_on: at the horizon, a declared shot, a pass in the air, a contest choice or a shot worth more than the possession is played on with the forcing replies only, at most extension_cap extra team turns (provisional). clear_reason: the choice from two depths earlier is kept unless the new best beats it by more than stable_margin, one standard error of the reading at the phase (provisional, D-120).
search._goals: Step 16, goals stage 4 (off; needs eval.advantages): turns that work on a top goal are searched first, and a position gains its goal potential (each attacker's best advantage worth, summed; 0 when the possession ends), the root's taken off.
